title: Claude can now test your app like a real user kopija

scenes.vo: Claude can now test your app like a real user.
scenes.notes:
Strong opening frame. Show Claude Code and a web app open in Chrome. Make it obvious that Claude is interacting with the app in the browser.

Keep it bold and clean. This is the promise.

scenes.vo: Manually clicking through your app after every change takes time, you still miss bugs, and honestly it gets annoying fast.
scenes.notes:
Show the painful workflow: code change, open app, click through pages, fill inputs, miss something, go back, test again.

This should feel repetitive and frustrating.

content.headline: Manual testing takes time. And you still miss things.

scenes.vo: Now Claude Code can connect directly to Chrome and do that testing for you.
scenes.notes:
Show Claude Code connected to Chrome. Browser is open with a local app ready to be tested.

Simple reveal frame. Don't overload it.

scenes.vo: And that means Claude can actually use your app, not just write code for it.
scenes.notes:
Intro card for the capabilities section. Could show a small browser visual with multiple action markers or icons around it.

Acts like a mini chapter break before the list.

scenes.vo: It can click buttons, move through pages, and fill out forms for you.
scenes.notes:
Show 3 quick action examples: button click, page navigation, form filling.

These should be very concrete. Good place for more energetic animation.

content.headline:
Click buttons
Open pages
Fill forms

scenes.vo: It can also check validation, inspect browser errors, and show you exactly what happened on screen.
scenes.notes:
Show validation message, browser console error, and a visible test flow happening on screen.

This is the more technical half of the benefits.

content.headline:
Check validation
Read errors
Show what happened

scenes.vo: To connect it, install the Claude Chrome extension, then start Claude Code with chrome enabled.
scenes.notes:
Quick setup sequence. Show the extension in Chrome and then terminal / Claude Code setup step.

Keep this fast. Enough to show the idea, not a full tutorial.

scenes.vo: Then you can simply ask Claude to test your app, for example: test the signup flow and tell me what breaks.
scenes.notes:
Screen recording of Claude Code receiving a prompt to test the signup flow on the local app.

Make the prompt readable. This is the 'I can try this too' moment.

content.headline:
Test the signup flow
and tell me what breaks.

scenes.vo: Now you can watch Claude click through the app, test the flow, and inspect the result live on screen.
scenes.notes:
Show Claude actively using the app in Chrome: clicking, typing, submitting, and checking the result.

This should feel like the strongest visual proof moment.

scenes.vo: Follow for more AI app building tips.
scenes.notes:
Clean ending frame. Keep Claude Code and Chrome theme, with simple follow CTA.

Short, clear, no extra explanation.

content.headline: Follow for more AI app building tips.
